ELI5: How New Horizons can send images of pluto back to earth in a matter of hours when it is billions of miles away?

Very simple. The data comes back as a radio transmission, which travels more or less (well, actually a little less) than the speed of light.

Pluto's current position in orbit places it about 4 light-hours from Earth.
Wow really? I seemed to have a slightly distorted understanding of how far a light-hour is and how far away everything is.
The average distance to Pluto from Earth is 5.64 light hours. And yes, radio transmission and light are part of the same family : electro magnetic waves. 1 light hour is 1.07925285 × 109 kilometers
Jeeeeee-sus. I had no idea that radio transmissions moved so fast. That's impressive.

If want to really burn your brain, look into binary golay code and turbo code. They go into how they compress and error correct the data to transmit at such low power and long distances without constant re-sends due to corruption. If you want to go further and are a math geek, multidimensional sphere packing is a wild area of study.

The constant 'c' is an ideal figure. If one reads the classical definitions1 closely, 'c' is defined as 'the speed of light in a vacuum'. Radio frequency radiation is not light, but it is close. Both light and radio are radiant electromagnetic energy, and both travel near 'c'. The reason I say near 'c' is that 'c' is an ideal, as previously mentioned; space is not a perfect vacuum so the actual measured speed will always be slightly less than 'c'.

[1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_of_light

New Horizons points straight at Earth and uses a microwave frequency (the same type found in cellphones and satellites) to transmit data. It sends the data in really small sizes to prevent corruption, and it takes the data about 4.5 hours to travel 3 billion miles. It transmits at speeds slower than dial-up, and will take 16 months to send all it's data to Earth.

Source: http://gizmodo.com/why-itll-take-new-horizons-16-months-to-send-us-this-we-1717769317

Recently, I watched "Expelled from Paradise," namely the English dub premiere at AX15 (rewatched on BD). All said, solid 4/5, would watch again. Warning, moderate spoilers below.

While I've yet to see the film in the original Japanese (felt like saving the experience for the theater), I can say that the English VA was acceptable. Steve Blum, as the voice of Dingo, and Johnny Bosch, voice of Frontier Setter, were spot-on with their performances. Wendee Lee's performance of Angela was passable, but suffered from a very obvious case of "Older woman trying to voice a teenager" syndrome. However, I'd like to give a special shoutout to Bosch: Frontier Setter stole the entire show, partially in thanks to his great delivery, and as a result he's now one of my favorite .

I mean (SPOILER IMAGE) LOOK AT THIS GUY

The animation quality was variable. Being entirely 3D, so far as I can tell, the show suffers from the same problems as Knights of Sidonia in that some sequences are seamless and fit the medium and some scenes look clunky and plastic. They get it right where it counts, though, namely the well-executed fight scenes

The first act does a good job of introducing us to the world organically, answering just enough questions without dipping into pointless exposition and leaving stuff open for speculation on a lot of fronts. Further, the first act features some pretty well executed storytelling vis a vis Spike Spiegel Dingo, with a few snippets of comedy thrown in. Maybe I'm just a Steve Blum fanboy, but something about his voice makes him perfect for the role of snarky, laid back cowboys. He and Wendee have some good chemistry, to boot, so Act 1 was pretty sound so far as a pseudo-mystery story goes.

The movie really comes into its own with Act 2, once Frontier Setter shows up. Starting off with a simultaneously anticlimactic and hilarious introduction of the "villain" as - who possibly has some relation to Space Core - the movie segues into a more action-scifi tone, which, between its animation style and its soundtrack, it pulls off fantastically. Expelled from Paradise is one of those movies where, once the action kicks up, it draws you in and takes you for a ride to the point that you laugh in glee at the fatalities and tricks that get pulled out during the fight. Along the way, it also manages to touch on some legitimate societal/technological questions, but it doesn't spend too much time focusing on the subject - personally I see it as a good thing, given that deep introspection wouldn't really fit the tone of the film. Good for thought experiments, though.

The soundtrack was pretty good - nothing to write home about a la a Hans Zimmer album, but it did its job in supporting the movie, which is all you can really ask for. It's a pretty generic mix of classical action scoring and some electronic sound, plus some rustic guitar tracks thrown in.

I can say that, unfortunately, the bloopers shown at the premier are not in the BD (unless I'm absolutely blind). I say unfortunately because Steve Blum delivering a heartfelt, emotional goodbye to a character he addresses as "Washing machine head" is goddamn hilarious. Once I have time, I'll probably give this another run-through for the subbed version just to get the full experience - I picked up the LEBD at AX for a steal.
